testedState.worktreeBinding: The diagnosis inputs are uncommitted and are bound individually by SHA-256 below.

consumedFailedAuthority.provenInterval: bootstrap-entered was durably published; module-entered was not published

provenFacts.fact: The production-equivalent emitted bundle has exactly two non-builtin package imports: ts-morph and typescript. No unexpected third-party external specifier is present.

The runtime plan uses the same two package names as recursive dependency-closure seeds and materializes every discovered package below .isolated-compiler/node_modules, which is an ancestor resolution location for the heavyweight core.

The inspected physical closure is ts-morph, typescript, @ts-morph/common, code-block-writer, minimatch, path-browserify, tinyglobby, brace-expansion, fdir, picomatch and balanced-match; each declared package entry exists and no native .node file is required by this closure.
All remaining emitted import specifiers are Bun-provided Node builtins, plus the function-local dynamic bun:ffi import. The scan does not prove AppContainer-time loader access or module evaluation.

staticReview.moduleEvaluationConclusion: rootCause=null; a manifest-bound staged loader is required

ambiguitySet: heavyweight core URL resolution or bundle parse/link failure
typescript package resolution or evaluation failure
ts-morph or its CommonJS dependency-closure resolution or evaluation failure
top-level evaluation of the unsplit bundled repository and third-party modules before the runner body
abnormal Bun loader/runtime termination in the bootstrap-entered to module-entered interval
rootCauseAvailability: The bounded scan proves there is no unexpected emitted third-party external and source inspection proves a matching physical dependency closure. Neither fact proves AppContainer-time package resolution, dependency evaluation, bundled top-level evaluation or runtime survival, so selecting one cause would be speculation.

smallestDeterministicSuccessor.authority: mutation-specific manifest-bound staged loader between bootstrap and heavyweight core
requirements: The loader is a tiny literal generated asset bound into the existing runtime destination manifest and plan revision.
It imports typescript and ts-morph sequentially before importing the sibling heavyweight core.
Each completed boundary is durably published using the existing finite path-free checkpoint protocol.
Caught imports expose no Error, message, path or output; failure remains a fixed coarse termination plus the last valid checkpoint.
The heavyweight core keeps module-entered as its first body action, so the final interval remains core linking or bundled top-level evaluation.
No generic AppContainer executor, pipeline, canonical Verification artifact, WorkspacePaths or success digest changes.

decision.next: Freeze a separate staged-loader implementation successor with finite dependency checkpoints and focused non-AppContainer sentinels.

invalidationRules: This diagnosis is bound to the exact manifest, failed vertical evidence, source hashes, package manifests, Bun version, head, tree and base recorded above.
A staged loader may refine the runtime interval but cannot convert vertical-v4 to PASS.
Any source change requires a separately frozen implementation manifest and new focused evidence; vertical-v4 must not be rerun under its terminal manifest.
